title: Īśā Upaniṣad
teaser: Seeing the entire universe enveloped by the Divine; acting with total engagement while renouncing clutching.
galleryNote: The shortest of the major Upaniṣads (18 verses), placed at the conclusion of the Saṃhitā itself, reconciling renunciation with worldly action.

title: Kena Upaniṣad
teaser: Who sends the mind to wander? De-centring egoic mastery by realizing the conscious presence behind every perception.
galleryNote: Opens with radical epistemological inquiry: that which cannot be thought by the mind, but by which the mind itself is cognized.

title: Kaṭha Upaniṣad
theme: The Sovereign Chariot & The Dialogue with Death
teaser: Nachiketa looks into the eyes of Death to choose the Good over the Pleasant, discovering the invincible rider within.
galleryNote: The classic dramatic dialogue set in the halls of Yama, containing the archetypal allegory of the Chariot and horses of sensory desire.

title: Praśna Upaniṣad
theme: Vitality & The Six Questions of Prāṇa
teaser: Six seekers interrogate sage Pippalāda on the origin of life, the distribution of breath, and conscious equanimity in crisis.
galleryNote: A dialogue exploring how prāṇa (vital breath) sustains psychosomatic resilience during severe stress and physical decline.

title: Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad
teaser: Two birds upon a single branch: one eats the bitter-sweet fruit, the other watches in radiant stillness.
galleryNote: Declares that the Self cannot be attained by the weak ('Nāyam ātmā balahīnena labhyaḥ') and establishes truth as the supreme trajectory.

title: Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad
theme: The Four States & The Silent Witness
teaser: A, U, M dissolve into Turīya: the fourth dimension of consciousness that remains unscarred across waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.
galleryNote: Consisting of merely twelve compact prose aphorisms, it forms the bedrock of non-dual psychology and meditative cognitive therapy.

title: Taittirīya Upaniṣad
teaser: Peeling through physical body, vital breath, mental reactivity, and intellect to the kernel of unconditioned bliss.
galleryNote: Systematizes human experience into the five koshas and provides the formula for overcoming fear: 'He who knows the bliss of Brahman fears nothing'.

title: Aitareya Upaniṣad
teaser: The eye sees, the ear hears, the heart feels—yet all cognitive faculties are sustained by a single undivided awareness.
galleryNote: One of the oldest Vedic Upaniṣads, source of the Great Saying (Mahāvākya) 'Prajñānam Brahma' (Consciousness is Brahman).

title: Chāndogya Upaniṣad
teaser: The Knower of the Self crosses beyond all sorrow: Uddālaka's banyan seed and Sanatkumāra's lesson on the Infinite.
galleryNote: A monumental text of ancient dialectic, containing 'Tat Tvam Asi' and the therapy of grief administered to scholar Nārada.

title: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad
theme: Fear Dissolves in Non-Duality & Dialectical Audacity
teaser: Fear arises only when a second is imagined; Yājñavalkya, Maitreyī, and Gārgī explore fortitude and the three syllables of thunder.
galleryNote: The 'Great Forest' Upaniṣad, unsurpassed in intellectual scale, home to the Asato Mā prayer and the debates of King Janaka's assembly.

title: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad
theme: The Fire of Meditation & Somatic Equanimity
teaser: Holding the chest, neck, and head erect, drawing sensory turbulence inward like an untamed chariot team brought to rest.
galleryNote: A bridge between classical Upaniṣadic metaphysics and early Yoga psychology, prescribing stillness of breath and body under pressure.

title: Maitrī Upaniṣad
teaser: The mind alone is the cause of human bondage and liberation: like fire settling into its hearth when fuel is withdrawn.
galleryNote: A late classical synthesis addressing existential fatigue, psychic burn-out, and the systematic training of the mental apparatus.
